chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira who said:

Muhammad ibn Abdullah said to al-Ridha (peace be upon him) while I was listening: 'My father narrated to me from his household, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that he said to one of them: In our lands there is a garrison post called Qazween, and an enemy called al-Daylam. So is there any jihad or ribat?'

So he (the Imam) said: 'It is upon you with this House (Kaaba), so perform its hajj.' Then he repeated the statement to him, and he (the Imam) said: 'It is upon you with this House (Kaaba), so perform its hajj.'

Is one of you not pleased that he may be in his home, spending upon his family from his earnings, awaiting our matter (the Rising)? If he attains it, he will be like one who was present at Badr with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). And if he dies while awaiting our matter, he will be like one who was with our Qa'im (peace be upon him) — like this — in his tent,' and he joined his two index fingers together. 'And I am not saying like this,' and he joined his index finger and middle finger, 'for this one is longer than this one.'
So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'He spoke the truth.'

key_terms.أمرنا: Our matter — a Shia eschatological reference to the Rising (Qiyam) of the Qa'im (Imam al-Mahdi)
key_terms.الديلم: al-Daylam — the Daylamite people of the Caspian highlands, frequently at odds with the Abbasid caliphate
key_terms.القائم: al-Qa'im — the Rising One, title for the Awaited Imam al-Mahdi (AS)
key_terms.رباط: Ribat — a frontier garrison post where soldiers are stationed to defend Islamic territory
key_terms.فسطاط: Fusṭāṭ — a large tent or camp pavilion, typically associated with military commanders
key_terms.قزوين: Qazween — a city in northwestern Iran near the Caspian Sea region, historically a frontier zone

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about jihad and the reward for awaiting the Qa'im?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a complex chain reaching Imam al-Ridha (AS), addresses the question of jihad and garrison duty at Qazween on the frontier with the Daylam people during the early Abbasid period. When questioned whether armed engagement with the Daylam enemy was obligatory, the Imam twice redirected the questioner to the Hajj pilgrimage instead of military duty. He then delivered a profound teaching: one who stays at home, cares for his family, and awaits the Rising of the Qa'im earns rewards equal to those who witnessed Badr with the Prophet (SAWW) or those who will be in the Qa'im's own tent — with the Imam dramatically demonstrating closeness by placing two index fingers side by side, not the slightly unequal arrangement of index and middle finger. Imam al-Ridha (AS) then confirmed the truthfulness of this tradition. The hadith reflects the Shia theological position that during the occultation, pious waiting and supporting one's family carries immense spiritual merit equivalent to battlefield participation.
